question.text: If the digits are not allowed to repeat in any number formed by using the digits <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo></math> then the number of all numbers greater than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>000</mn></math> is equal to __________.

solution.text:
We have to form a number greater than 10,000 by using the digits 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, hence, the first place of the number can't be zero.

Thus, for the first place we have 4 choices i.e. 2, 4, 6, 8 and the remaining places can be filled with any of the digits, thus we have respectively 4, 3, 2, 1 choices.

Hence, using the fundamental principle of multiplication, the total numbers which are greater than 10,000 are

=4×4×3×2=96.
